label: start
name: starting architecture
last_analysis: All nine trials scored 0 on dev and had 0 training success. That covers the starting net, the layer scorer, the conv+FC hybrid and a plain MLP, each with low-entropy, high-entropy, 1-epoch and slow recipes. Changing the recipe alone did not move the score, and nothing has shown a signal above noise. My best guess is that greedy exact builds need precise per-placement checks that the current heads cannot compute well. To place a brick correctly, the net must find the footprint's landing layer, the maximum column height under the footprint. Then it must check, for every footprint cell, that the target has a cell at that layer and no empty target gap below it. Pooling min, max and mean over the footprint, as the PoolHead does, cannot express this two-stage dependency. In this last round I test a head that does the two stages explicitly: pool learned landing features over the footprint, then judge each footprint cell with a shared MLP and pool the judgements. The three candidates use different recipes and inputs.
